subject: Post-call: capacity envelope & latency targets (Hosted vs Dedicated)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Harris <jamie@brightretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: capacity envelope & latency targets (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Jamie — thanks for the convo earlier. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we have alignment before we scope a pilot: 

Summary of what you shared
- Peak QPS: 340 requests/sec for product search ranking fan-out (95th pct).
- Typical payload: 512 tokens average per request (search context + query).
- 95th pct latency target: 150ms end-to-end (from app to token stream start).
- SLA sensitivity: yes — seasonal peaks (Black Friday) must be covered; predictable capacity required for checkout flows.

High-level deployment guidance (first pass)
- Dedicated capacity is the conservative recommendation if BrightRetail wants single-tenant GPUs for predictable 95th pct latency at sustained 340 QPS and tight SLOs.
- Hosted API can meet lower steady-state/variable workloads with RB (reserved burst) and prefix caching, but may require a hybrid approach (Hosted + Dedicated fallback) for predictable peak capacity.

Open questions we need to close to finalize recommendation
1) Can you share % of requests that are <200 tokens vs >200 tokens (affects batching efficiency)?
2) What is your desired RTO for a regional outage — are you ok with automatic fallback to another region?
3) Do you have strict data residency or VPC requirements for search logs?

Attachments: latency_requirements_summary.pdf (your notes we took this morning), MAP_v0.3.pdf (mutual action plan draft)

Suggested immediate next steps
- Technical deep-dive (45–60m) with your infra/ops + our Solutions Engineer (Ben) — propose Wed 17th, 9am PT.
- We’ll run a quick capacity calculation and deliver two options: (A) Dedicated sizing + cost, (B) Hosted with burst/fallback cost and performance tradeoffs.
- Post-deep-dive: 2-week pilot scope if you want to validate traffic shape on test harness.

Can you confirm Wed 17th 9am PT or propose an alternate? If you can share the token distribution and any regional constraints ahead of the call that’ll let Ben size accurately.

Thanks,
Olga
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199

Thanks, Olga — solid summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token distribution: approx 70% of requests are under 180 tokens; 25% in the 180–600 token range; 5% >600 tokens.
- Regional constraints: EU logs must remain in EU for GDPR; primary customers (US) are in us-west and us-east. We expect to run EU traffic in a separate region.
- RTO expectation: for checkout flows, we need <5 minutes RTO for failover. For non-critical analytics, longer is acceptable.

We’re open to Dedicated for checkout and Hosted for lower-criticality ranking; curious on the cost delta and how quickly we can ramp Dedicated for Black Friday. 

Wed 17th at 9am PT works for us. I’ll invite our infra lead (Laurence) to the technical deep-dive.

—Jamie

Jamie / Olga — digging into the numbers you gave. Quick technical notes and ballpark sizing assumptions (high level):

- With 70% <=180 tokens, effective average token length moves down from 512 to ~260 tokens for batching calculations. That materially improves throughput and reduces per-token latency due to better batching.
- For sustained 340 QPS at ~260 tokens avg: we estimate ~4 x A100-class GPUs for Dedicated to hit 95th pct ~120–140ms (model-dependent). This assumes 8k context and standard KV cache hit rates.
- Hosted route: to hit 95th pct ~150ms at 340 QPS you’d need a dedicated reservations commitment or a multi-instance scaling policy with aggressive warm pool. Hosted alone without reservations is higher risk for Black Friday spikes.

Attachments: redwood_capacity_calc.xlsx (workbook with QPS->GPU mapping, assumed batching curves, and a quick cost model). I attached a shaded sheet recommending 4x GPU for steady state and headroom of +30% for bursts.

Proposal for Wednesday deep-dive
- Agenda: traffic profile (10m), token distribution validation (10m), failure modes & fallback policy (10m), Dedicated sizing walkthrough + Hosted fallback design (20m).
- Outcome: we’ll agree on pilot target (20k QPS minutes simulated), deliver a Dedicated sizing + pilot quote within 48 hours of the call.

If EU residency is required for logs, Dedicated in EU region or Private VPC with on-prem log forwarding are plausible. We should capture that as a hard requirement on the MAP.

Ben

Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast follow. Confirming next steps and owners so BrightRetail has a clear action plan: 

1) Wed 17th, 9am PT — Technical deep-dive (Ben to lead). Calendar invite sent; Laurence + infra team confirmed.
2) Ben to deliver Dedicated sizing + pilot quote within 48 hours after the deep-dive (deliverable: sized config, estimated costs, pilot runbook). Owner: Ben.
3) Olga to update MAP_v0.3 with residency flag (EU logs) and pilot acceptance criteria; deliver updated MAP within 24 hours after deep-dive. Owner: Olga.
4) If BrightRetail commits to Dedicated pilot, we’ll spin reserved capacity and provide a sandbox endpoint for the pilot within 5 business days of PO.

Risks / contingencies
- If traffic shape is heavier on long-tail tokens (>600) than projected, Dedicated GPU count may increase; we’ll capture this as a scope delta in the MAP.
- For Regional residency / <5m RTO for checkout, Dedicated in-region + cross-region failover policy recommended.

Thanks — see you Wed. I’ll attach the updated MAP and Ben’s calc after the call.
